title: invoke-shim: incremental schema-stripper and adaptive streaming invocation helpers
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Problem: SDKs currently validate function/tool schemas eagerly and strictly at call-site which causes poor ergonomics for streaming/resumable invocations and makes progressive upgrades of schemas hard. This ticket proposes an "incremental schema-stripper" approach paired with a small set of invocation helpers (dry-run, streaming-resume, backpressure-aware retries) usable in Python/TS/Go SDKs.
acceptance_criteria: A small library that can take a full function schema and produce a lenient runtime validator that only enforces required fields while allowing additional keys for forward-compatibility
SDK binding helpers: dry_run_invoke, stream_resume_invoker, and backpressure_retry that composes with existing request/response middlewares

Cross-language examples in python, typescript, and go showing: a) schema-less partial arguments accepted, b) streaming resume after transient network failure, c) retries that respect server-side token consumption metrics
Unit tests for validator combinators and integration tests against local runtime mock
A RFC-style design doc linked and an initial PR opened for review
work_items: Design draft for incremental validation model (conformance + permissive fallback)
Port combinator to TS + Go with identical runtime semantics
Implement dry_run_invoke to perform a zero-token validation path and return a deterministic invocation plan
Implement stream_resume_invoker that checkpoints KV-cache pointers and replays tokens until resume
Add backpressure-aware retry policy that consults X-Token-Consumed header and max_in_flight setting
Benchmarks comparing strict vs incremental validation latency for warm cold calls
comments: 2025-02-28 Aisha Patel: Created ticket after discussion with SDK team. Problem observed during user study: integrating new function schemas led to repeated hotfixes because LLM responses include extra fields.

2025-03-01 Marco Rivera: Spike complete for Python combinator. Prototype stored at https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-prototypes/pull/72. Prototype shows ~0.8ms overhead for permissive validator vs 1.6ms for strict full coercion on common payload sizes.

2025-03-02 Yuki Tanaka (review): Feedback: ensure the permissive validator emits a best-effort coercion report for telemetry (not just allow/deny). Also flagged edge-case where streaming resume needs to reconcile partial structured outputs.

2025-03-03 Marco Rivera: Updated plan to include 'coercion_report' metadata on invocation objects; added 'max_unvalidated_depth' option to combinator for low-trust environments. Draft PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/2104

2025-03-04 Priya Singh (pm): Approved scope for Cycle 2025-W09. Please include migration guide for customers pinning strict schemas. Also mark ticket for security review because invocation helpers touch auth headers and KMS flow.

2025-03-04 Marco Rivera: Triage note: security_review_required=true, added unit tests and flagged dependency ENG-94210 for streaming backpressure metrics integration. Planning to open platform integration PR next week.
notes: Testing: add interop test that runs python/ts/go example against local mock runtime (mock at tools/mock-runtime)
